output.title: Tool use before automation: pick one workflow first
output.body:
If you have tried ChatGPT but have not tied it to a real workflow yet, the first question is not which AI tool to buy. It is which repeatable job in the business to connect first.

Pick one workflow that happens every week and has a clear output: customer replies, invoice data entry, lead qualification, or something similar. Then map it on paper before you automate anything. Write down three things: what enters the workflow, where the manual steps happen, and what decision rule is being used.

That mapping usually shows whether the problem is tool integration or the work itself. If your email, CRM, documents, and other SaaS tools are still disconnected, improve the tool chain first. That is often the cheaper thing to test. If the workflow already runs through connected tools and still depends on repeatable rules, AI may have a sensible place.

Be explicit about the approval gate. If the work depends on your judgment, say so. If your approval is the control point, keep it there. Human approval stays mandatory for money movement and other high-risk decisions.

The goal is not to force AI into every process. The goal is to find one bounded workflow where the handoffs are clear and the next step is obvious. The tricky part is usually not the model; it is the plumbing.
